analysis.investment_thesis: A tiny INR 30 Cr micro-cap custom e-learning shop with ROE of just 0.45% — earning essentially nothing on shareholder capital despite a deceptively low 7.96x P/E. No visible moat, no institutional conviction (FII 0.04%, DII 0%), and well outside my circle of competence for a business I can bet on 10 years forward.
key_strengths: Low headline P/E of 7.96 suggests no froth
Debt situation not flagged — capital-light services model
key_risks: ROE of 0.45% is catastrophic — capital is being destroyed vs. a risk-free rate
Micro-cap (INR 30 Cr) custom-learning vendor with zero discernible moat or pricing power
Near-zero institutional ownership signals no independent due-diligence validation
red_flags: ROE <1% inconsistent with a P/E of 8 — earnings base is razor thin and fragile
Recently listed SME-style name with no long-term track record of compounding
Commoditized IT-enabled services segment with low switching costs
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The single most important number here is ROE of 0.45%. A business that can only earn less than half a percent on its equity base is not creating value — a bank deposit does dramatically better with zero risk. The low P/E of 7.96 is a value trap: it is low precisely because the earnings are trivial in absolute terms on a INR 30 Cr market cap. Custom learning development is a fragmented, project-based services business with no recurring revenue contracts disclosed, no brand moat, and no scale advantage over hundreds of similar Indian vendors.

Promoter holding of 69.28% is fine, but by itself it is not an investment thesis — plenty of promoters own most of mediocre businesses. With essentially zero FII/DII interest, a micro-cap float, and an unproven post-listing track record, this sits squarely outside my circle of competence and well below my bar for a "wonderful business at a fair price." I'd pass without a second look.
